name: Battle of Sedan (1870)

sides.name: Prussian and allied Third and Fourth Armies

phases.title: The French held a ring round Sedan
phases.text: MacMahon placed the 7th Corps on the north-west crest, the 1st Corps facing east and the 12th Corps in Bazeilles, with the 5th Corps in reserve in the centre. The Germans closed a ring round the north-west, west and east.

phases.title: The Bavarians storm Bazeilles
phases.text: A Bavarian brigade crossed the Meuse on pontoon bridges in the morning mist and rushed Bazeilles. The French fought from stone houses while Bavarian guns shelled the buildings.

phases.title: The 8th Division arrives and Bazeilles is stormed again
phases.text: The Prussian 8th Infantry Division arrived at 08:00. Von der Tann had not been able to bring artillery to bear from long range, so he committed his last brigade to storm the town, supported by guns across the Meuse.

phases.title: Wimpffen attacks the Saxons at La Moncelle
phases.text: Ducrot ordered a retreat but Wimpffen overruled him and threw his forces against the Saxons at La Moncelle. The French rallied briefly, drove back the artillery around the village and pressed the Saxons.

phases.title: The French counter-attack collapses
phases.text: With Bazeilles taken and fresh waves of Prussian troops arriving, the French counter-attack began to collapse. The 8th Infantry Division was sent to reinforce the fighting at La Moncelle.

phases.title: The 22nd Division turns Douay's left flank
phases.text: Douay's left flank was dug in above Floing and its fire kept the Germans out of the village. By 13:00 the French artillery there had been defeated and the German 22nd Division turned the flank, defeating French counterattacks.

phases.title: French cavalry charge at Floing
phases.text: Ducrot sent Margueritte's cavalry to open an escape route with three attacks on Floing, where the XI Corps stood. Margueritte was mortally wounded in the first charge and German infantry fire defeated the other two.

phases.title: German infantry reach the Calvaire and the French break
phases.text: By 14:00 German infantry stood on the Calvaire and attacked from all sides. The 7th Corps broke, seeking refuge in the Bois de la Garenne or Sedan, and the 1st Corps was routed by Saxon and Guards artillery.

phases.title: The Guards take the Bois de la Garenne
phases.text: The Bois de la Garenne was under German artillery fire from several sides. When the Prussian Guards infantry captured the wood at 14:30, the French troops inside it surrendered.

phases.title: A last attack after the white flag
phases.text: Napoleon III hoisted a white flag on the walls of Sedan. Wimpffen refused to surrender and launched one more attack, which the Germans defeated.

note: The accounts give directions only roughly (north-west, west, east, south-west). The places are set by judgement on that basis, and the Meuse, the wood and the hills are drawn only as markers; the accounts do not say exactly where each lay. They also name the Bavarian attacks both at Bazeilles and as coming from the south-west, which cannot be shown together.
